ci-bot: [ALERT] Pipeline failed on main after merge (PR #9876 by @jason). Failed step: smoke-gpu (matrix-run 3/3). <https://ci.redwood.example/runs/2345|view run>

maria-velasquez: who can grab this? smoke-gpu is blocking main.

jason: that's my PR — sorry folks. I ran the usual tests locally but didn't hit the GPU matrix. I can take it now.

kyle: pinging @jason + @maria-velasquez. Maria, can you try a quick rerun first (usually flakes)?

maria-velasquez: rerunning now: `./ci rerun pipeline 2345`

ci-bot: Rerun started: build 2345.2.

ci-bot: build 2345.2 FAILED — smoke-gpu step errored. Relevant log snippet:

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "runtime/engine/decoder.py", line 412, in step
    kv_cache = kv_cache_load(state)
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory when allocating tensor (size=256MB)
During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
  File "tests/smoke_gpu/test_smoke.py", line 23, in <module>
    run_smoke()
RuntimeError: decode_step failed after 12 tokens
```

sarah: hmm that looks like an allocation spike in decode. Not a simple flaky timeout. @ben any recent infra changes touching kv cache or kernel selection?

ben: I didn't touch kv_cache directly, but I merged a tiny attention-kernel heuristic tweak earlier today (PR 9880). Could be related.

jason: I touched the routing that picks kernels for short sequences — possibly correlated. I can roll back locally and trigger a rerun.

kyle: if it's a regression, we should bisect. Simple plan: try a quick revert on main (temporary) and rerun smoke. If that passes, revert PR and follow up.

maria-velasquez: quick check in logs shows allocation spike right at `decode_step` start, consistent across runs.

jason: pushing revert candidate branch now: `git push origin HEAD:revert-9876-temp` and requesting CI.

ci-bot: Build 2345.3 triggered by jason/revert-9876-temp.

oncall: I've paused automerge and blocked the autobot for main until triage finishes. :white_check_mark:

ci-bot: Build 2345.3 PASSED — smoke-gpu succeeded.

kyle: ok good signal. Revert candidate fixed the smoke run. Next: open a revert PR, hold automerge, and create an issue to debug the attention kernel vs kv cache interaction.

jason: opening revert PR now and will add notes. I'll take ownership of the follow-up with @ben. Sorry for the disruption — thanks for the quick eyes.

maria-velasquez: adding minimal repro steps + log links to the issue. Marking this triaged for now.

ci-bot: Note: main automerge remains paused until revert PR lands and is approved.

kyle: thanks all — assigning follow-up to @jason and @ben. If anything else fails, please re-alert this thread.
